```{r setup}
library(rscprep)
library(Seurat)
```

Attaching metadata columns that inform information like treatment group, genotype, timepoint
and any other sample-level information have to get attached to the objects manually.
 `includeMetadata()` does that from a sample-level table, keyed on the names of the list
`seuratFrom10x()` returns.

## The workflow

```{r workflow}
seurat_list <- seuratFrom10x(
  path        = "/path/to/Pool1/outs",
  multi = TRUE
)

names(seurat_list)
#> [1] "Bleo_18_Slim_10" "Bleo_22_Slim_14" "Ctrl_04_Slim_02" "Ctrl_09_Slim_07"
```

Those names are what you key on. Write a sheet against them:

```{r sheet}
sheet <- data.frame(
  Sample    = c("Bleo_18_Slim_10", "Bleo_22_Slim_14",
                "Ctrl_04_Slim_02", "Ctrl_09_Slim_07"),
  Treatment = c("Bleomycin", "Bleomycin", "Control", "Control"),
  Timepoint = c("D21", "D21", "D21", "D21")
)

annotated <- includeMetadata(seurat_list, sheet)
#> ✔ Added 2 metadata columns to 4 objects: "Treatment" and "Timepoint"
```

In practice this sample sheet can live in your folder as a csv and be read in directly.

```{r csv}
sheet     <- read.csv("samplesheet.csv")
annotated <- includeMetadata(seurat_list, sheet)
```

Each column is broadcast across every cell of its sample, so after merging you
can group by it directly:

```{r merged}
merged <- mergeSeurat(annotated)
table(merged$Ident, merged$Treatment)
```
